name: Silhouette Illustration
visualIdentity: Normalized from an explicit flat black silhouette description. Communicates through recognizable outlines, poses, and negative space, using solid color layers and clear depth. Details may be omitted when forms read; limbs stay separated and contrast remains sufficient during movement.
suitableUses: Explicit good fits include product and editorial introductions, explanatory or illustrated narratives, and abstract or cinematic sequences with meaningful chapters. Also suits symbolic storytelling alone. These are suitability cues, not limits on the source definition.
limitations: Adapt or omit chapter transitions when a topic is too short, transitions obscure causality, or cuts conflict with a continuous-shot or loop requirement. Avoid overlapping silhouettes, gradients, fast moves, type over figures, and busy motion. Preserve readable copy and negative space.
palette: Use a limited set of discrete solid colors; the optional suggestion for new artwork is background #F5E9CF, foreground #253442, accent #647F81. These are not canonical: task, brand, approved reference, existing semantic mappings, and asset colors take precedence. Preserve exact values, role assignments, color families, and color-count limits; do not recolor or add hues. Gradients are disabled. Suggested text on the accent misses normal-text contrast; use the main background or another existing contrasting backing, then check actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Use filled contours, designed pose groups with explicit pivots, masks, and consistent luminance for depth. Keep authored movement smooth where useful, while preserving deliberate cuts, impacts, holds, or stepped exposure. Optional chapter transitions coordinate outgoing/incoming states and copy across a bounded, reversible progress window; storytelling may map scroll to meaningful stages. For video, schedule these states on seekable composition time with reading holds; interactive HTML may use finite scroll progress and needs usable static or reduced-motion states. Ensure direct and backward seeks restore coherent states. Keep one owner per animated property.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Suggest music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence from the subject, audience, narrative, and explicit audio requirements; do not assume assets exist. Synchronize picture and sound to shared time, preserve speech intelligibility, avoid clipping, and inspect them together.
assetRequirements: Use task-provided or authorized artwork, copy, fonts, and audio; load local assets and fonts before rendering. SVG is recommended for scalable contours and masks; Paper.js is optional for vector paths and compound silhouettes, with holes, winding, overlaps, morph correspondence, and SVG fidelity checked. Canvas 2D is an alternative. Keep rest geometry immutable and evaluate states from composition time; bake or deterministically replay stateful motion.
combinations: Works strongly alone for symbolic narratives. Optional depth layering (style-101) adds planes while keeping silhouettes readable; use limited solid tones and stable outlines. Optional title typography motion (style-093) places real-text titles in negative space, using the primary palette and a slow rhythm. Avoid overlap, added accents, gradients, and busy movement. Chapter transitions and scroll storytelling are optional patterns, only when supported by the scene and narrative.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion engine by visual fidelity and action; SVG/Paper.js and GSAP are suggested, while Motion is optional and requires verified seeking. HyperFrames is the primary scene, timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export pipeline. Remotion is allowed only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required output; record the reason. Pipeline tools do not replace style rendering. For video, validate representative frames and decoded playback, including dimensions, duration, frame rate, synchronization, and loop continuity.
